canonical.title: Find Median from Data Stream
canonical.sourceFilePath: 09. Heaps/3. Hard Problems/05. Median in a stream.cpp

narrative.title: The Toll Plaza Flow Gauge
narrative.scenario: A toll plaza logs one vehicle count per hour and regulators request the running median after every reading — the hourly figure splitting all readings into equal halves. The gauge never re-sorts: it keeps the lower half of readings in a max-topped vault and the upper half in a min-topped vault, rebalancing after each insert so the medians are always one or two tops away.
narrative.inputFormat: A list of operations: ["add", value] or ["findMedian"].
narrative.outputFormat: Return the list of medians produced by every findMedian operation, in order.

testCases.explanation: Two readings split the median halfway; the third reading makes 2 the true middle.
Each median is the middle of {5}, then {1,5,15} → 5... specifically 5, 10, 5.

hintLevels: Level 1: Split the data into a smaller half and a larger half; the median lives at their boundary.
Level 2: A max-heap guards the lower half, a min-heap the upper half; keep sizes within one.
Level 3: Route each new value through both heaps (push low, hoist the max to upper, rebalance) — the invariant maintains itself.
